conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with: **How many children do you have, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I have two children. Alex is 16 and Blake is 8.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have Alex who is 16 and Blake who is 8.

Let me ask you some questions to determine your eligibility:

**First, do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand a bit more about Alex, who is 16.

**Is Alex still in approved education or training (such as school, college, or an approved training program)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in college doing A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, that's helpful to know. Now let me ask about your living arrangements:

**Do both Alex and Blake live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, they both live at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I need to ask about work and benefits for Alex:

**Is Alex working for 24 hours or more per week, or claiming any benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working that much and doesn't claim any benefits.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for either Alex or Blake?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! And one final question to complete the assessment:

**Are either of the children fostered, or are you looking after them under any arrangement with the local council that provides payment towards their accommodation or maintenance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of them are fostered and I'm not getting any payments from the council.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for both Alex and Blake.**

Here's the breakdown:

**For Blake (age 8):** You're eligible because Blake is under 16, lives with you in the UK, and you're responsible for their care.

**For Alex (age 16):** You're also eligible because even though Alex is 16, they are still in approved education (A-levels at college). Child Benefit can continue for young people under 20 who stay in approved education or training, as long as they're not working 24+ hours per week or claiming benefits in their own right - which Alex is not.

Since no one else is claiming Child Benefit for either child and there are no special arrangements with the local council, you meet all the criteria to claim Child Benefit for both children.

**Please note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit but may need to pay back some or all of it through your tax return.
